name: Sintra
subcategory: AI employee suite for small business
tagline: A pack of persona-branded AI assistants that do marketing, support, and admin busywork for small businesses.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Sintra is essentially a prompt library with mascots: a dozen named 'AI employees' that each wrap a set of task templates around a frontier model. The core loop, pick a role, pick a task, fill in a form, get output, is a weekend build on top of an API key, and you get to skip the markup. What you cannot one-shot cheaply is the accumulated prompt engineering across hundreds of business tasks, plus the integrations that let assistants actually post to your social accounts, read your inbox, or touch your store. Also missing: the persistent brand memory that makes outputs stop sounding generic after the tenth use, which is mostly just a well-maintained context file you would have to write yourself. If you already have API access and taste, the DIY version is genuinely fine. If you wanted the assistants to do things rather than draft things, it is not.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with role-based assistants, each holding a system prompt plus a library of task templates, that calls an LLM API with your saved brand context and keeps a searchable history of outputs.
requirements: An LLM API key (OpenAI or Anthropic)
Node and a local database (SQLite is fine)
Willingness to write your own task prompts
Per-integration OAuth work if you want posting or inbox access
whatYouLose: Hundreds of pre-written task prompts you did not have to think up
Integrations that let assistants publish, email, or pull store data instead of just drafting text
A polished UI and mobile access without you maintaining it
Any hand-holding when the outputs are bad
Shared updates as models change underneath
moatNotes: The moat is packaging and onboarding, not technology. It sells confidence to people who do not want to write prompts.
whyPeopleStillPay: Most Sintra customers are not paying for capability, they are paying to not stare at an empty chat box. The personas and task menus convert a general-purpose model into something a busy shop owner can use on a Tuesday without learning anything, and that framing is worth real money to people whose time is better spent elsewhere. The DIY replacement is technically straightforward and practically demanding: you become the prompt author, the maintainer, and the support desk. If that sounds like a hobby rather than a chore, build it.
notes: The mascots are free, the prompt library is the product, and you can write your own in an afternoon if you are honest about your own business.
prompt:
Build a local-first "AI staff" web app: a set of role-based assistants that run task templates against an LLM API, with a shared brand context.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, schema created on first run
- Anthropic or OpenAI SDK, model and key from .env
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost, no auth, no telemetry, no cloud

Data model:
- brand: one row holding company name, what we sell, audience, tone notes, things to never say
- assistant: name, role (for example Copywriter, Support, Social, Analyst), system prompt, emoji
- task: belongs to an assistant, title, description, prompt template with {{placeholders}}, list of input fields (label, type: text or textarea or select with options)
- run: task id, filled inputs as JSON, output text, model, created_at, pinned boolean

Features in scope:
- Sidebar listing assistants, clicking one shows its task cards
- Task page renders a form from the task's input fields, submits, streams the model response into the page
- Every prompt sent includes the brand row plus the assistant system prompt as context
- Save every run to history, with search across inputs and outputs, and a pin toggle
- "Refine" button on any output: send the output back with a free-text instruction to revise
- Editor screens to create and edit assistants and tasks, so the prompt library is user-owned
- Copy-to-clipboard and markdown rendering of outputs
- Seed the database with 4 assistants and 3 tasks each so it is usable immediately

Explicitly out of scope:
- No social posting, email sending, or third-party OAuth
- No multi-user accounts, billing, or hosting config
- No vector database, no RAG, no file uploads

Deliver a README with setup steps, a .env.example with the API key variable, and honest notes on what the app cannot do.
